zh.prompt: 期末老师宣布「考试绝对公平」：同卷、同时、同标准阅卷。但患阅读障碍的小明申请延长 50% 时间，老师拒绝：「给他特权，对别的同学就不公平。」家长群里也有人附和。这里被争来争去的「公平」，究竟指规则完全一致，还是结果绝对对等？请在校准尺上标出它的合理范围。
hints: 「公平」在此藏着真歧义，不是非黑即白
给阅读障碍者延长时长，可能恰恰是为了机会对等
想清你捍卫的是形式齐一，还是实质对等
zh.explanation: 「公平」在这里是一个真歧义：一端把它等同于规则对每个人都一模一样，另一端等同于每个人都拿到相同结果。但给阅读障碍者延长时长，可能恰恰是为了「规则面前机会对等」。校准时要想清：你捍卫的，是形式的齐一，还是实质的对等？这正是灰度的关键。

en.prompt: At finals the teacher declares 'the exam is absolutely fair': same paper, same time, same grading. But Xiaoming, who has a reading disability, asks for 50% extra time; the teacher refuses, saying 'that privilege would be unfair to others.' Parents in the group chat agree. The 'fairness' being argued over — does it mean perfectly identical rules, or perfectly equal outcomes? Mark its reasonable range on the scale.
hints: Here 'fairness' hides a real ambiguity, not a black-and-white
Extra time for a reading disability may itself be about equal opportunity
Clarify whether you defend formal uniformity or substantive parity
en.explanation: Here 'fairness' is a genuine ambiguity: one end equates it with rules identical for everyone, the other with identical outcomes for everyone. Yet giving extra time to a reading-disabled student may precisely serve 'equal opportunity before the rules.' When calibrating, ask which fairness you defend — formal uniformity or substantive parity. That is the heart of gray thinking.
